chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's *slutans* (authority) is not absolute but conditional upon human free will and voluntary submission to his whispers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle that believers retain agency, as Satan only gains dominion over those who choose to follow his guidance, thereby preserving divine justice and the possibility of spiritual elevation through conscious obedience.
